groups.instructions: Match each finding with the correct researcher, A–C. You may use any letter more than once.

questions.prompt: showed that birds learn which part of the night sky stays fixed
questions.explanation: Emlen's indigo buntings learned 'the point around which the night sky appears to rotate'.

questions.prompt: changed the apparent direction of a light source to test birds' responses
questions.explanation: Kramer 'used mirrors to shift the apparent position of the sun'.

questions.prompt: found evidence of an inherited map based on magnetism
observed that birds lost their sense of direction in cloudy weather
questions.explanation: Kramer's starlings 'became disoriented under overcast skies'.

groups.instructions: Complete the sentences below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

questions.prompt: Using the sun as a compass requires an internal ________.
Each location on Earth has a distinctive magnetic ________.
One theory suggests birds detect magnetism through a protein called ________ in the eye.
Shearwaters may use ________ carried by the wind to find their colonies.
Young birds that are blown off course often fail to ________ for it.
questions.explanation: 'they often fail to correct for it'.

questions.prompt: Why is a compass alone 'not enough for true navigation'?

options.text: It does not work at night.
It does not show the animal's position relative to its goal.
It can be affected by magnetic fields.
Young animals cannot learn to use it.

questions.explanation: An animal also needs 'a way of knowing where it is in relation to its goal'.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about the two theories of magnetic detection?
questions.explanation: 'The two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive'.

questions.prompt: Experiments with homing pigeons suggest that

options.text: smell helps them navigate from unfamiliar places.
they rely mainly on the stars.

questions.explanation: Pigeons with blocked smell 'have greater difficulty returning home from unfamiliar release sites'.

questions.prompt: Why does the writer mention artificial lighting in the final paragraph?

options.text: to explain how scientists study birds at night
to show human activity may disrupt navigation
to describe a new navigation method

questions.explanation: Human factors 'may all interfere with the cues on which migrating animals depend'.
